newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal/Spain yield gap creates arbitrage space.
newsitem.headline: Portugal/Spain yield gap creates arbitrage space.

text.p: The significant yield premium at which Portuguese shorter term bonds are trading compared with their Spanish equivalents creates opportunities for arbitrage as the gap should narrow, analysts and traders say.

The sources said that the 15 to 20 basis point positive spread between Portuguese (OT) and Spanish government bonds (Bonos) with a life of up to four years was unjustified on the basis of the two countries' relative economic performance.
A spread of below 10 basis points would be sufficient to cover the usual liquidity premium that is levied against the smaller Portuguese market, they said.
"The big spreads between the OT and Bonos, between two and four years, do not make any sense. At the very most, they should be 10 basis points," said Fincor analyst Pedro Andrada.
"The spreads open a wide front for arbitrage with Spain. It is right at this point to buy OTs and sell Bonos," said a fixed-income trader who declined to be named.

The spread between the February 1998 OT and the October 1998 Bono stands at 20 basis points, the same as the gap between the March 1999 OT and April 1999 Bono, while the gap between the April 2000 OT and the March 2000 Bono is 15 basis points.

In contrast, the spread between the two countries' benchmark 10-year cash bonds is a negative 17 basis points. The Portuguese bond is outperforming the 10-year Bono, trading at a yield of 7.57 percent against 7.73 percent for the Spanish paper.
Analysts said that the market was giving too much importance to the fact that Bank of Spain official money rates were below those of Portugal.
They said that the trend in money rates in both countries was similar and the Bank of Portugal probably had more room than its Spanish counterpart to cut rates further.
When the Bank of Spain cut its repurchase pact rate 50 basis points to 6.75 percent last week, the Bank of Portugal only lowered 15 basis points to 7.10 percent.
Overnight and tomorrow/next rates in Portugal are around 7.02-7.06 percent, against 6.90-92 percent in Spain. Six-month money is at 6.78-6.85 percent against 6.72-6.80 percent.
"The Bank of Portugal has room to cut the repo, and as soon as this happens, the price of the OTs is going to rise. It is a good bet," said Andrada.

The analyst said that the Portuguese economy was looking in better shape than Spain's and that the country was also better placed when it came to qualifying for the European Union's planned single currency.
"The Bank of Portugal, after the budget, should cut (the repo) again and by the end of the year, we expect a repo rate under seven percent," said an analyst at an investment bank.
"Everything points to us not having reached the end of the cycle on lower yields," he added.
Just as the 10-year OT will have to narrow the negative spread with Spain, so the short and medium bonds will have to reduce the positive spread," he said.
Only the timing was in doubt. "If a non-resident believes in our convergence (with Europe), he can correct the curve in less than half an hour," the analyst said.
